verifications.claim: As of late March 2026, the average 30-year fixed mortgage rate is approximately 6.38% to 6.56%
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "The average rate for a 30-year fixed mortgage was 6.38%" (R2); "6.36%" as of 03/23 (R3); "6.57%" (R6); "6.64% for top-tier" (R7); "6.47%" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources report averages in late March 2026 falling within or very close to the claimed range.

verifications.claim: As of late March 2026, the average 30-year fixed mortgage rate marks a four-week increase to the highest level since September 2025
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "rose for the fourth straight week to the highest level since September" (R2); "highest point since September 2025" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated in R2 as fourth straight week; R6 confirms six-month high since September 2025.

verifications.claim: 30-year fixed mortgage rates have risen from February lows below 6%
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "falling below 6% in late February" (R2); "touching below 6% in February" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly confirm rates were below 6% in February and have since risen.

verifications.claim: Freddie Mac Weekly Average 30-year fixed mortgage rate for the week of March 29, 2026 is 6.38%
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Freddie Mac said ... 6.38% this week" (R2, March 26); "Freddie Mac’s weekly data ... 6.38%" (R7, March 29)
verifications.reasoning: Direct attribution to Freddie Mac at 6.38% for the relevant late March week.

verifications.claim: Freddie Mac Weekly Average 30-year fixed mortgage rate the previous week was 6.22%
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "up from 6.22% last week, Freddie Mac" (R2); "up from 6.22% the week before" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Exact previous week figure directly from Freddie Mac in both sources.

verifications.claim: Bankrate Daily Survey 30-year fixed mortgage rate for the week of March 29, 2026 is 6.56%
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "Weekly national average: 6.50%" "for the week of March 29th"; "current average ... 6.57%" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Bankrate (R6) reports weekly national average 6.50% and daily 6.57% around that week, close but not exactly 'Daily Survey 6.56%'.

verifications.claim: Mortgage News Daily 30-year fixed mortgage rate for the week of March 29, 2026 is ~6.64% for top-tier borrowers
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Mortgage News Daily, its lender index ... 6.64% for top-tier borrowers" (R7, March 29)
verifications.reasoning: Exact match including source, date, value, and 'top-tier borrowers' qualifier.

verifications.claim: The increase in rates has slowed mortgage application demand
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "Total mortgage applications dropped by 10.5%" after rate increase (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Direct link between rate rise and application drop supports claim, though causation is implied not explicit.

verifications.claim: Rates are following the 10-year Treasury yield
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "mortgage rates are more directly tied to the yield on the 10-year Treasury Bond" (R3); "Mortgage rates tend to follow the 10-year Treasury yield" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Explicit statements in sources confirm the relationship.

verifications.claim: Some forecasts anticipate rates to hover around 6.1% to 6.3% throughout 2026
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "Bankrate projects ... around 6.1%"; "could also rise to 6.5%" (R3); "near 6.10% through the end of 2026" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Forecasts cite ~6.1%/6.10% with broader possible range, supporting but not precisely matching 6.1-6.3% hover.

verifications.claim: The average 30-year refinance rate is roughly 6.78%
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "today's average 30-year refinance interest rate is 6.78%" (R6, April 1 referencing recent)
verifications.reasoning: Direct exact match for average 30-year refinance rate.
